newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Semiconductor index left behind.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Semiconductor index left behind.

text.p: Trading in options on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's (PHLX) Semiconductor Index failed to keep up with the hectic pace in some of the underlying issues, traders said Tuesday.
"There's not a lot going on in there today," one trader at the PHLX said of semiconductor index options trading.
"It's traded a couple thousand (contracts). That's not remarkable volume," he added.
Traders said investors appeared to be focusing more on the index's stocks, several of which saw fairly sharp moves and heavy volume.
By 1420 CST/2020 GMT, the index was down 1.88 points, or 0.75 percent, at 250.40, well off its intraday high of 257.72, which marked a new high for the year.

The index and its components received a boost early Tuesday on news late Monday that the industry's benchmark indicator, the book-to-bill ratio, rose to 1.15 in November from a revised 1.11 in October.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index is made up of 16 stocks of companies involved in the design, manufacture, distribution and sale of semiconductors.
Among the 16, only four were in positive territory in late trading, led by flagship Intel Corp, which was up 1-1/8 at 131-1/4 on heavy volume of more than nine million shares.
Six Intel options made the list of most active calls on the American Stock Exchange. The Intel December 130 call traded about 5,350 contracts.
The most active semiconductor index options was the December 250 put, which traded about 700 contracts. Right behind it was the December 250 call, which traded roughly 600.
The December 250 put was ahead 3/4 at six and had open interest of 125 through Monday. The December 250 call lost 1-1/8 to 6-5/8. Its open interest was 203.
The trader at the PHLX said activity was mixed, with some investors buying calls and others buying puts to protect portfolios. He said there was not a great sense of bullishness.
Volatilities were fairly stable, he added.
He said activity in semiconductor index options had been slow for the past couple of months.
Outside of Intel, the other three semiconductor index components still posting gains by late trade were Advanced Micro Devices, Motorola Inc and Texas Instruments Inc.
Texas Instruments was up 3/4 at 67-3/8 on 2.04 million shares after reaching a new year high of 68-1/4.
Motorola added 3/8 to 55-3/8 on 3.65 million shares. It had reached 56-1/4.
Advanced Micro was up 1/2 at 21-3/4, just off its 21-7/8 session high. Turnover topped 1.18 million shares.
